---- MODULE W4Od2m6p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Zones, MaxCapacity, MaxClock, LeaseDuration, NULL

VARIABLES leaseOwner, leaseExpiry, capacity, clock

vars == <<leaseOwner, leaseExpiry, capacity, clock>>

\* leaseOwner[r] is the zone r currently leases, or NULL if r holds no lease.
\* capacity[z] is mutable at runtime (the twist): ChangeCapacity may raise or
\* lower it, but a lowering is only accepted down to the zone's current usage.

ActiveCount(z) == Cardinality({r \in Robots : leaseOwner[r] = z})

TypeOK ==
    /\ leaseOwner \in [Robots -> Zones \union {NULL}]
    /\ leaseExpiry \in [Robots -> 0..(MaxClock + LeaseDuration)]
    /\ capacity \in [Zones -> 0..MaxCapacity]
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock

Init ==
    /\ leaseOwner = [r \in Robots |-> NULL]
    /\ leaseExpiry = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ capacity = [z \in Zones |-> MaxCapacity]
    /\ clock = 0

RequestLease(r, z) ==
    /\ leaseOwner[r] = NULL
    /\ ActiveCount(z) < capacity[z]
    /\ leaseOwner' = [leaseOwner EXCEPT ![r] = z]
    /\ leaseExpiry' = [leaseExpiry EXCEPT ![r] = clock + LeaseDuration]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, clock>>

ReleaseLease(r) ==
    /\ leaseOwner[r] # NULL
    /\ leaseOwner' = [leaseOwner EXCEPT ![r] = NULL]
    /\ leaseExpiry' = [leaseExpiry EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, clock>>

ExpireLease(r) ==
    /\ leaseOwner[r] # NULL
    /\ leaseExpiry[r] <= clock
    /\ leaseOwner' = [leaseOwner EXCEPT ![r] = NULL]
    /\ leaseExpiry' = [leaseExpiry EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, clock>>

\* A capacity change is rejected if it would drop below the zone's current usage.
ChangeCapacity(z, newCap) ==
    /\ newCap \in 0..MaxCapacity
    /\ newCap >= ActiveCount(z)
    /\ capacity' = [capacity EXCEPT ![z] = newCap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseExpiry, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseExpiry, capacity>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, z \in Zones : RequestLease(r, z)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : ReleaseLease(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : ExpireLease(r)
    \/ \E z \in Zones, c \in 0..MaxCapacity : ChangeCapacity(z, c)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: active lease count per zone must never exceed its current (mutable) capacity.
CapacityNeverExceeded ==
    \A z \in Zones : ActiveCount(z) <= capacity[z]

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2, r3}
    Zones = {z1, z2}
    MaxCapacity = 2
    MaxClock = 2
    LeaseDuration = 1
    NULL = NULL

INVARIANT CapacityNeverExceeded
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a set of storage zones, each with a bounded
capacity for how many robots may be actively working inside it at once. A
robot may only enter a zone by acquiring a lease on it; the lease binds the
robot to that zone until the robot releases it explicitly or the lease
expires after a fixed duration measured against a shared discrete clock. A
robot with no active lease holds no zone. Leases can only be granted while
the zone still has room under its currently configured capacity, and a
robot may drop its lease at any time before expiry through an explicit
release action, in addition to the automatic expiry action once the
clock has passed the lease's expiry time. The twist is that zone capacity
is not fixed: an operator can reconfigure a zone's capacity up or down at
runtime (for example to close off part of a zone for maintenance or reopen
it), and a capacity reduction is only accepted if it does not drop the
allowed capacity below the number of robots currently holding an active
lease in that zone, so the fleet is never left in violation of a newly
lowered limit. The clock advances independently as a fifth action, up to a
bounded horizon. The full action set is: RequestLease (a robot with no
lease acquires a lease on a zone that has spare capacity), ReleaseLease (a
robot with an active lease voluntarily gives it up), ExpireLease (a robot's
lease is cleared once the clock has reached or passed its expiry time),
ChangeCapacity (an operator sets a zone's capacity to a new value, rejected
if the new value is below that zone's current active-lease count), and
Tick (the shared clock advances by one step, bounded by a maximum horizon).
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, for every zone, the number of
robots currently holding an active lease on that zone never exceeds that
zone's currently configured capacity, even as capacity is changed at
runtime. (Disclosure: this invariant is a direct count-vs-capacity bound,
which is the literal property under test here -- the twist is that the
bound it is checked against, capacity[z], is itself a runtime-mutable
variable rather than a fixed constant, and the ChangeCapacity guard is
exactly the mechanism that must be verified to preserve the bound.)

---- MODULE W4Od13m8p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS R1, R2, Slots, None

Requesters == {R1, R2}

VARIABLES netLock, fineLock, owner, held, request

vars == <<netLock, fineLock, owner, held, request>>

\* Hierarchical locking: a customer must take the coarse network lock before
\* the fine per-slot lock, then commit the allocation and release the coarse
\* lock. An admin may reassign any already-allocated slot at any time,
\* bypassing that protocol, clearing any outstanding requests for that slot.

TypeOK ==
  /\ netLock \in Requesters \cup {None}
  /\ fineLock \in [Slots -> Requesters \cup {None}]
  /\ owner \in [Slots -> Requesters \cup {None}]
  /\ held \subseteq (Requesters \X Slots)
  /\ request \in [Requesters -> Slots \cup {None}]

Init ==
  /\ netLock = None
  /\ fineLock = [s \in Slots |-> None]
  /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> None]
  /\ held = {}
  /\ request = [r \in Requesters |-> None]

Submit(r, s) ==
  /\ request[r] = None
  /\ owner[s] = None
  /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![r] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<netLock, fineLock, owner, held>>

AcquireNet(r) ==
  /\ request[r] # None
  /\ netLock = None
  /\ netLock' = r
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, owner, held, request>>

AcquireFine(r) ==
  /\ netLock = r
  /\ request[r] # None
  /\ owner[request[r]] = None
  /\ fineLock[request[r]] = None
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![request[r]] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<netLock, owner, held, request>>

Grant(r) ==
  /\ netLock = r
  /\ request[r] # None
  /\ fineLock[request[r]] = r
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![request[r]] = r]
  /\ held' = held \cup {<<r, request[r]>>}
  /\ netLock' = None
  /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![r] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED fineLock

\* A customer holding the coarse lock whose target slot was taken by a
\* faster rival, or whose request was cancelled by an admin override while
\* it waited, releases the coarse lock and drops the stale request instead
\* of blocking the network lock forever.
Abort(r) ==
  /\ netLock = r
  /\ \/ request[r] = None
     \/ (request[r] # None /\ owner[request[r]] # None)
  /\ netLock' = None
  /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![r] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, owner, held>>

Release(r) ==
  /\ \E s \in Slots :
       /\ owner[s] = r
       /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = None]
       /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = None]
       /\ held' = held \ {<<r, s>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<netLock, request>>

\* Admin override only ever touches an already-allocated slot, and cancels
\* (rather than silently strands) any pending request that named that slot,
\* so no customer is left waiting forever on a slot the admin reassigned.
AdminOverride(s, r) ==
  /\ owner[s] # None
  /\ owner[s] # r
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = r]
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = r]
  /\ held' = (held \ {<<owner[s], s>>}) \cup {<<r, s>>}
  /\ request' = [x \in Requesters |-> IF request[x] = s THEN None ELSE request[x]]
  /\ UNCHANGED netLock

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Requesters, s \in Slots : Submit(r, s)
  \/ \E r \in Requesters : AcquireNet(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requesters : AcquireFine(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requesters : Grant(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requesters : Release(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requesters : Abort(r)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, r \in Requesters : AdminOverride(s, r)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(AcquireNet(R1))
  /\ SF_vars(AcquireNet(R2))
  /\ SF_vars(AcquireFine(R1))
  /\ SF_vars(AcquireFine(R2))
  /\ SF_vars(Grant(R1))
  /\ SF_vars(Grant(R2))
  /\ SF_vars(Abort(R1))
  /\ SF_vars(Abort(R2))

\* Safety: a customer's local acknowledgment of holding a slot must always
\* agree with the network's authoritative owner record for that slot -- this
\* rules out two different customers both being allocated the same slot.
HeldOwnerCoherence ==
  \A r \in Requesters, s \in Slots : <<r, s>> \in held => owner[s] = r

\* Liveness: no submitted request is left pending forever, whether it is
\* granted through the lock protocol or cleared by an admin override.
RequestsServiced == \A r \in Requesters : (request[r] # None) ~> (request[r] = None)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  R1 = R1
  R2 = R2
  Slots = {s1, s2}
  None = None
INVARIANT HeldOwnerCoherence
PROPERTY RequestsServiced
nl:
A vending machine network coordinates two customers competing for a shared
pool of product slots. To allocate a slot, a customer first takes a single
coarse network-wide lock, then takes the fine-grained lock on the specific
slot it wants, and only then commits the allocation, releasing the coarse
lock so the next customer can proceed. The full action set is: a customer
submits a request for a slot it currently believes is free; a customer with
a pending request acquires the coarse network lock once it is free; a
customer holding the coarse lock acquires the fine lock on its requested
slot, but only while that slot is still unallocated; a customer holding
both locks is granted the slot, which records it as the authoritative owner
and releases the coarse lock; a customer holding the coarse lock whose
requested slot turns out to already be taken -- because a rival customer
won the race for it, or because an admin cancelled the request while it
waited -- releases the coarse lock and drops the stale request instead of
blocking the network forever; a customer that owns a slot may release it,
clearing both the ownership record and the fine lock; and a privileged
admin may, at any time and without taking either lock, override the
allocation of any currently allocated slot, reassigning it to a different
customer and cancelling any outstanding request either customer had
pending for that same slot. SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a customer's own
record shows it holds a given slot, the network's authoritative allocation
record for that slot must agree the same customer owns it, so the same
slot is never allocated to two different customers at once, even across an
admin override. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every submitted allocation request is
eventually resolved -- granted to its requester through the coarse-then-
fine locking protocol, cancelled because an admin override reassigned that
slot, or dropped because the requester discovered the slot was already
taken and released the network lock.

---- MODULE W4Od4m5p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Participants, Quorum, MaxRound

Rounds == 1..MaxRound

VARIABLES round, authorized, sent, delivered, executed, credits

vars == <<round, authorized, sent, delivered, executed, credits>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in Rounds
  /\ authorized \subseteq Participants
  /\ sent \subseteq (Participants \X Rounds)
  /\ delivered \subseteq (Participants \X Rounds)
  /\ executed \subseteq Rounds
  /\ credits \subseteq (Participants \X Rounds)

Init ==
  /\ round = 1
  /\ authorized = Participants
  /\ sent = {}
  /\ delivered = {}
  /\ executed = {}
  /\ credits = {}

\* Votes are tagged with the round they were cast for and queue in the
\* network, which may deliver them out of order (the reordering twist).
Send(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ sent' = sent \cup {<<p, round>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, authorized, delivered, executed, credits>>

Deliver ==
  \E m \in sent :
    /\ delivered' = delivered \cup {m}
    /\ sent' = sent \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, authorized, executed, credits>>

AdvanceRound ==
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, sent, delivered, executed, credits>>

\* A revoked controller's already-credited votes can never be undone, and a
\* revocation may never strip the pool below the size needed for a quorum.
Revoke(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ Cardinality(authorized) > Quorum
  /\ ~ \E r \in executed : <<p, r>> \in credits
  /\ authorized' = authorized \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, sent, delivered, executed, credits>>

Execute ==
  /\ round \notin executed
  /\ \E Q \in SUBSET authorized :
       /\ Cardinality(Q) >= Quorum
       /\ \A p \in Q : <<p, round>> \in delivered
       /\ executed' = executed \cup {round}
       /\ credits' = credits \cup {<<p, round>> : p \in Q}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, authorized, sent, delivered>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Send(p)
  \/ Deliver
  \/ AdvanceRound
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Revoke(p)
  \/ Execute

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No executed round may be backed by an unauthorized or stale (wrong-round) vote.
SafetyInvariant ==
  \A r \in executed :
    LET CreditedParticipants == {p \in Participants : <<p, r>> \in credits}
    IN /\ Cardinality(CreditedParticipants) >= Quorum
       /\ CreditedParticipants \subseteq authorized
       /\ \A p \in CreditedParticipants : <<p, r>> \in delivered

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Participants = {p1, p2, p3}
  Quorum = 2
  MaxRound = 2
INVARIANT SafetyInvariant
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line moves vehicles through wash stations one round at a
time. Before the conveyor is allowed to advance to the next station for the
current round, a quorum of the currently authorized station controllers must
vote to approve the move. Controllers send their approval vote for whatever
round is current when they cast it, and the vote travels across the shop's
wireless network to the central conveyor controller. That network can reorder
messages in flight: a vote cast during an earlier round can be delayed and
arrive after the conveyor has already moved on to a later round, and a
revocation of a controller's authorization (for example when a controller
goes offline for maintenance) can likewise race with that controller's
in-flight vote instead of arriving before it. The system supports five
actions: a controller casting a vote for the round that is current when it
sends the message, the network delivering some pending vote out of order,
the conveyor advancing to the next round once the current round's action has
resolved, an authorized controller being revoked (only once none of its
votes have already backed a completed advance, so the audit trail of
completed advances is never invalidated after the fact), and the conveyor
executing the advance for the current round once a quorum of currently
authorized controllers have delivered votes tagged for that exact round.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every round the conveyor has executed is backed by at least
a quorum of controllers that are still authorized and whose credited votes
were genuinely delivered and tagged for that exact round, so no advance is
ever credited to a controller who was unauthorized or whose vote was stale
(reordered in from a different round).

---- MODULE W4Od3m6p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS i1, i2, MaxLease, MaxEpoch

Instances == {i1, i2}
NoOne == "None"

VARIABLES holder, epoch, ttl, pending, settledBy

vars == <<holder, epoch, ttl, pending, settledBy>>

\* Lease-based ownership: an instance may only BEGIN settling the shared
\* batch while it holds a live (unexpired) lease; completion is guarded by
\* an epoch stamp so a reclaimed (stale) attempt can never be credited once
\* the shared pool has re-issued the lease to another instance.
\* AuthorizedSettlement: whoever is credited with settling the batch must
\* still be its recorded lease holder -- rules out unauthorized/stale credit.

Init ==
  /\ holder = NoOne
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ ttl = 0
  /\ pending = [inst |-> NoOne, ep |-> 0]
  /\ settledBy = NoOne

AcquireOp(i) ==
  /\ ttl = 0
  /\ settledBy = NoOne
  /\ holder' = i
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ ttl' = MaxLease
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, settledBy>>

Acquire1 == AcquireOp(i1)
Acquire2 == AcquireOp(i2)

BeginOp(i) ==
  /\ holder = i
  /\ ttl > 0
  /\ pending.inst = NoOne
  /\ settledBy = NoOne
  /\ pending' = [inst |-> i, ep |-> epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, ttl, settledBy>>

Begin1 == BeginOp(i1)
Begin2 == BeginOp(i2)

CompleteSettle ==
  /\ pending.inst # NoOne
  /\ pending.ep = epoch
  /\ settledBy' = pending.inst
  /\ pending' = [inst |-> NoOne, ep |-> 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, ttl>>

AbortStale ==
  /\ pending.inst # NoOne
  /\ pending.ep # epoch
  /\ pending' = [inst |-> NoOne, ep |-> 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, ttl, settledBy>>

Tick ==
  /\ ttl' = IF ttl > 0 THEN ttl - 1 ELSE 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, pending, settledBy>>

Next ==
  \/ Acquire1 \/ Acquire2
  \/ Begin1 \/ Begin2
  \/ CompleteSettle
  \/ AbortStale
  \/ Tick

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(Acquire1) /\ SF_vars(Acquire2)
  /\ SF_vars(Begin1) /\ SF_vars(Begin2)
  /\ SF_vars(CompleteSettle) /\ SF_vars(AbortStale)
  /\ WF_vars(Tick)

AuthorizedSettlement ==
  settledBy # NoOne => holder = settledBy

EventualSettlement == <>(settledBy # NoOne)

StateBound == epoch <= MaxEpoch

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  i1 = i1
  i2 = i2
  MaxLease = 2
  MaxEpoch = 6
INVARIANT AuthorizedSettlement
PROPERTY EventualSettlement
CONSTRAINT StateBound
nl:
A bank runs two independent settlement-processing instances that draw on one
shared pool holding the lease for a single interbank settlement batch. Before
either instance may act on the batch it must acquire a time-bounded lease from
the shared pool: the lease carries an expiry countdown (a "ttl") and each
newly granted lease is stamped with a fresh epoch number. Only the instance
currently recorded as the lease holder may begin settling the batch, and it
may only begin while its lease has not yet expired (ttl > 0). Because the pool
is shared between the two instances, once a lease genuinely expires (ttl
reaches 0) either instance may reclaim it, which bumps the epoch and hands the
batch to whichever instance next acquires it. An in-flight settlement attempt
records the epoch it observed when it began; if the lease is reclaimed under a
new epoch while that attempt is still outstanding, the attempt is now stale
and can never be credited -- it must instead be discarded so a fresh attempt
by the batch's current lease holder can proceed. The full action set is:
Acquire1 and Acquire2 (instance 1 or instance 2 takes an expired, unsettled
batch's lease from the pool and starts a new epoch), Begin1 and Begin2 (the
current, unexpired lease holder stamps a new in-flight settlement attempt with
the epoch it currently observes), CompleteSettle (an in-flight attempt is
credited to its instance only if the epoch it observed still equals the
batch's current epoch), AbortStale (an in-flight attempt whose observed epoch
no longer matches the current epoch is discarded, freeing the batch for a
fresh attempt), and Tick (the lease countdown decrements toward expiry, or
idles once already expired). SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the batch is credited
as settled to some instance, that instance is still the batch's recorded
lease holder at that moment and remains so forever after, so settlement
credit can never be given to an unauthorized instance or to one whose claim
has gone stale under a reclaimed lease. LIVENESS PROPERTY: the batch is
eventually settled.

---- MODULE W4Od7m2p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, Capacity, MaxOverrides

VARIABLES yardCount, phase, votes, override, overrideCount

vars == <<yardCount, phase, votes, override, overrideCount>>

\* Two-phase commit governs admission of a container into the bounded-
\* capacity crane yard: every participant must vote "yes" during the
\* preparing phase before an ordinary Commit is allowed. A privileged admin
\* can force a Commit without unanimous consent, but the yard-capacity guard
\* below still applies on that path -- the invariant checks the override
\* never lets the yard overflow.

AllVoted    == \A p \in Participants : votes[p] # "none"
AllVotedYes == \A p \in Participants : votes[p] = "yes"
SomeVotedNo == \E p \in Participants : votes[p] = "no"

Init ==
  /\ yardCount = 0
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ votes = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
  /\ override = FALSE
  /\ overrideCount = 0

StartPrepare ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ phase' = "preparing"
  /\ votes' = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
  /\ override' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardCount, overrideCount>>

CastVote(p) ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ votes[p] = "none"
  /\ \E v \in {"yes", "no"} : votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardCount, phase, override, overrideCount>>

Commit ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ AllVoted
  /\ AllVotedYes
  /\ yardCount < Capacity
  /\ yardCount' = yardCount + 1
  /\ phase' = "committed"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, override, overrideCount>>

Abort ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ SomeVotedNo
  /\ phase' = "aborted"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardCount, votes, override, overrideCount>>

\* Unanimous consent alone is not enough: if the yard is already at capacity
\* when every participant has voted yes, the coordinator aborts instead of
\* stalling -- there is always a resolution once voting completes.
AbortNoRoom ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ AllVoted
  /\ AllVotedYes
  /\ yardCount = Capacity
  /\ phase' = "aborted"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardCount, votes, override, overrideCount>>

\* Admin override: bypasses the unanimous-consent rule but not the capacity
\* guard, and is itself rate-limited by MaxOverrides to bound the state space.
AdminOverrideCommit ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ ~AllVotedYes
  /\ overrideCount < MaxOverrides
  /\ yardCount < Capacity
  /\ yardCount' = yardCount + 1
  /\ phase' = "committed"
  /\ override' = TRUE
  /\ overrideCount' = overrideCount + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED votes

ResetTx ==
  /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardCount, votes, override, overrideCount>>

ContainerDeparts ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ yardCount > 0
  /\ yardCount' = yardCount - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, override, overrideCount>>

Next ==
  \/ StartPrepare
  \/ \E p \in Participants : CastVote(p)
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort
  \/ AbortNoRoom
  \/ AdminOverrideCommit
  \/ ResetTx
  \/ ContainerDeparts

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: the number of containers physically in the yard must never exceed
\* the yard's bounded capacity, even along the admin-override path.
CapacityInvariant == yardCount <= Capacity

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Participants = {p1, p2, p3}
  Capacity = 3
  MaxOverrides = 2

INVARIANT CapacityInvariant
nl:
In a container-ship crane yard, cranes admit containers into a storage area
of bounded capacity. Admission of each container is coordinated by a
two-phase commit protocol across the yard's participants -- the crane
operator, the yard controller, and the ship's manifest system: the
coordinator opens a preparing phase and asks every participant to cast a
vote, and only commits the admission once every participant has voted yes.
If any participant votes no, the admission aborts instead. A privileged yard
administrator may invoke an override that forces a commit without waiting
for unanimous consent from the participants, bypassing the normal voting
requirement entirely -- but the override still respects the yard's physical
capacity limit, so a container is only ever moved in when there is room,
whether the commit came from ordinary consensus or from the override. Once a
transaction is settled (committed or aborted), the yard resets to idle and
is ready for the next admission attempt. Containers already resting in the
yard may also depart, freeing capacity for future admissions. If every
participant has voted yes but the yard is already at capacity by the time
voting completes, the coordinator aborts instead of stalling, so a
resolution always exists once voting finishes. The admin override is itself
rate-limited, so only a bounded number of overrides can occur over the
yard's lifetime, preventing uncontrolled bypass of the normal protocol. The
full action set is: starting a new admission round, a participant casting
its vote, committing on unanimous consent, aborting on any dissenting vote,
aborting because the yard has no room left despite unanimous consent, the
admin's override commit, resetting after a settled transaction, and a
container departing the yard.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Even when the privileged admin exercises the override to
force an admission through without unanimous participant consent, the
number of containers physically present in the crane yard never exceeds its
bounded capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m0p2t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, NoDrone, UnitBalance, Amounts, MaxVersion

ASSUME NoDrone \notin Drones
ASSUME UnitBalance \in Nat
ASSUME MaxVersion \in Nat
ASSUME Amounts \subseteq (Nat \ {0})

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET d == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN  f[d] + SumOver(f, S \ {d})

TotalFuel == SumOver([d \in Drones |-> UnitBalance], Drones)

\* Version stamps saturate at MaxVersion so the reachable state space stays finite.
Bump(v) == IF v < MaxVersion THEN v + 1 ELSE v

VARIABLES balance, version, req, retries

vars == <<balance, version, req, retries>>

NoReq == [active |-> FALSE, from |-> NoDrone, to |-> NoDrone, amt |-> 0, ver |-> 0]

Init ==
  /\ balance = [d \in Drones |-> UnitBalance]
  /\ version = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ req = NoReq
  /\ retries = 0

\* Optimistic locking: Propose stamps the version read at the source.
Propose ==
  /\ ~req.active
  /\ \E d1, d2 \in Drones, amt \in Amounts :
       /\ d1 # d2
       /\ balance[d1] >= amt
       /\ req' = [active |-> TRUE, from |-> d1, to |-> d2, amt |-> amt, ver |-> version[d1]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version, retries>>

Patrol(d) ==
  /\ version[d] < MaxVersion
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![d] = Bump(@)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, req, retries>>

\* Lock check succeeds: fuel only moves between drones, it never appears or vanishes.
CommitTransfer ==
  /\ req.active
  /\ version[req.from] = req.ver
  /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![req.from] = @ - req.amt, ![req.to] = @ + req.amt]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![req.from] = Bump(@)]
  /\ req' = NoReq
  /\ retries' = 0

\* Lock check fails: retry instead of abort, so a slow (never failed) drone still converges.
RetryTransfer ==
  /\ req.active
  /\ version[req.from] # req.ver
  /\ req' = [req EXCEPT !.ver = version[req.from]]
  /\ retries' = retries + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version>>

Next ==
  \/ Propose
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Patrol(d)
  \/ CommitTransfer
  \/ RetryTransfer

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(CommitTransfer) /\ WF_vars(RetryTransfer)

\* SAFETY invariant: total reserve is conserved; LIVENESS: every request clears.
FuelConserved == SumOver(balance, Drones) = TotalFuel

nl:
A small wildfire drone surveillance swarm patrols a burn perimeter and shares a common pool of battery/fuel reserve units so that no drone runs dry while another is over-provisioned. When a drone needs more reserve, it proposes an optimistic-locking transfer: it reads the source drone's current version stamp, computes the amount to move, and submits the request tagged with that stamp. Independently, any drone may log a local patrol update, which bumps its own version stamp (this is bounded so the system stays finite). When the in-flight transfer request is finally checked against the source drone's version, two things can happen. If the version still matches what the requester read, the optimistic lock succeeds: the transfer commits, the requested amount moves from source to destination, and the source's version stamp advances. If the version has since changed because of an intervening patrol update, the lock check fails; rather than aborting, the requester retries by re-reading the source's current version and resubmitting the same request. A drone whose transfer keeps losing the race can be slow to converge -- it may need several retries before its request finally commits -- but it is never treated as failed and its request is never dropped: the retry loop keeps making progress until the lock check succeeds. Only one transfer request is in flight across the swarm at a time. The full action set is: Propose (create a new transfer request when none is in flight), Patrol (a drone bumps its own version stamp, up to a small cap), CommitTransfer (the lock check matches, so the request applies and clears), and RetryTransfer (the lock check fails, so the request re-reads the version and tries again).

SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state the sum of all drones' reserve units equals the swarm's initial total, since a transfer only moves reserve between two drones and never creates or destroys it, even while retries are outstanding or a drone's convergence is slow.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every transfer request that becomes active is eventually cleared (committed), so a slow-but-not-failed drone's request is never left pending forever.

VARIABLES leader, enrolled, pending, crashed, submitted

vars == <<leader, enrolled, pending, crashed, submitted>>

\* Leader election with failover: a crashed leader relinquishes leadership and
\* any surviving server may then be elected. Registration requests sit in an
\* unordered pool, modelling network reordering -- the leader may admit or
\* reject any pending request regardless of submission order.

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Servers \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ enrolled \subseteq Students
    /\ pending \subseteq Students
    /\ crashed \subseteq Servers
    /\ submitted \subseteq Students

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ enrolled = {}
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ submitted = {}

Submit(s) ==
    /\ s \in Students
    /\ s \notin submitted
    /\ submitted' = submitted \cup {s}
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, enrolled, crashed>>

\* The leader may admit any pending request -- reordering means submission
\* order gives no guarantee about processing order -- as long as a seat is
\* still free.
Admit ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ leader \notin crashed
    /\ pending # {}
    /\ Cardinality(enrolled) < Capacity
    /\ \E m \in pending :
        /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {m}
        /\ pending' = pending \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, crashed, submitted>>

\* A full course rejects a pending request outright rather than growing the
\* enrolled roster past capacity.
Reject ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ leader \notin crashed
    /\ pending # {}
    /\ Cardinality(enrolled) >= Capacity
    /\ \E m \in pending :
        pending' = pending \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, enrolled, crashed, submitted>>

Crash(s) ==
    /\ s \in Servers
    /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {s}
    /\ leader' = IF s = leader THEN NoLeader ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, pending, submitted>>

\* Failover: once the leader has crashed, any surviving server may take over.
\* The new leader inherits the already-committed enrolled set, so no capacity
\* bookkeeping is lost or duplicated across the handover.
Elect(s) ==
    /\ s \in Servers
    /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ leader' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, pending, crashed, submitted>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students : Submit(s)
    \/ Admit
    \/ Reject
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Crash(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Elect(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityNeverExceeded == Cardinality(enrolled) <= Capacity

nl:
A university course-registration system runs a single course section with a
fixed seat capacity. A small cluster of registrar servers coordinates
enrollment: at any time at most one server is the acting leader, and only the
leader may admit or reject registration requests. Students submit
registration requests, which are buffered by the system as an unordered pool
rather than a queue -- the campus network can reorder messages in transit, so
the leader has no guarantee that requests are ever handed to it in submission
order and must be prepared to admit or reject any pending request regardless
of when it was originally submitted. The leader can crash at any time; if the
crashed server was the leader, leadership reverts to vacant. Failover then
lets any surviving, non-crashed server be elected as the new leader, and the
new leader inherits the already-committed set of enrolled students exactly as
it stood at the crash, so no seat bookkeeping is lost or duplicated across the
handover. The system supports five actions: a student submitting a
registration request (Submit), the leader admitting a pending request into an
open seat (Admit), the leader rejecting a pending request because the course
is full (Reject), a server crashing and, if it was the leader, vacating
leadership (Crash), and a non-crashed server being elected leader while the
role is vacant (Elect). Because requests can be processed out of order and
leadership can hand off mid-stream, the system must still never let the
enrolled roster grow past the course's seat capacity, regardless of how
requests were reordered or how many times leadership failed over.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of students enrolled in the course never exceeds
its fixed seat capacity, even though registration requests may be admitted
out of submission order and leadership may fail over between servers.

\* A car-wash conveyor line admits queued cars via two-phase commit across
\* its stations: a round only commits once every station has prepared, and a
\* station may be arbitrarily slow to vote but never fails or is skipped.
\* CapacityCoherence ties the occupied-count bound to vote hygiene: the
\* conveyor stays within capacity and no round's votes linger once idle.

CONSTANTS Participants, Capacity, MaxQueue

VARIABLES queueLen, count, txStatus, votes

vars == <<queueLen, count, txStatus, votes>>

NoVotes == [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]

Init ==
    /\ queueLen = 0
    /\ count = 0
    /\ txStatus = "idle"
    /\ votes = NoVotes

CarArrives ==
    /\ queueLen < MaxQueue
    /\ queueLen' = queueLen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, txStatus, votes>>

StartAdmit ==
    /\ txStatus = "idle"
    /\ queueLen > 0
    /\ count < Capacity
    /\ txStatus' = "preparing"
    /\ queueLen' = queueLen - 1
    /\ votes' = NoVotes
    /\ UNCHANGED count

Prepare ==
    /\ txStatus = "preparing"
    /\ \E p \in Participants :
        /\ ~votes[p]
        /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queueLen, count, txStatus>>

Commit ==
    /\ txStatus = "preparing"
    /\ \A p \in Participants : votes[p]
    /\ count < Capacity
    /\ count' = count + 1
    /\ txStatus' = "idle"
    /\ votes' = NoVotes
    /\ UNCHANGED queueLen

Depart ==
    /\ count > 0
    /\ count' = count - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queueLen, txStatus, votes>>

Next == CarArrives \/ StartAdmit \/ Prepare \/ Commit \/ Depart

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(StartAdmit) /\ WF_vars(Prepare) /\ WF_vars(Commit)

CapacityCoherence ==
    /\ count <= Capacity
    /\ (txStatus = "idle" => votes = NoVotes)

CONSTANTS
    Participants = {p1, p2, p3}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxQueue = 2
INVARIANT CapacityCoherence
PROPERTY AdmissionProgress
nl:
On a car-wash conveyor line, cars first join a waiting queue before they may
enter the wash bays. Admitting a car onto the conveyor is governed by a
two-phase commit protocol run across the line's participant stations (rinse,
soap, and dry): when a car is waiting and no admission round is already in
progress, the line manager opens a round and asks every station to prepare.
Each station casts its prepare vote independently and in any order; a station
may be slow to respond -- taking arbitrarily many steps before it votes -- but
it is never failed and always eventually casts its vote. Only once every
station has prepared does the round commit, admitting the car onto the
conveyor and incrementing the occupied count; the round then resets so a new
one can begin. Independently of the commit protocol, a car that has finished
washing may exit the conveyor at any time, freeing a slot. The conveyor has a
fixed capacity and a commit is only permitted while free capacity remains.
The full action set is: a car arriving into the waiting queue, the line
manager opening an admission round, a station casting its prepare vote, the
round committing and admitting the waiting car, and a finished car departing
the conveyor.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of cars on the conveyor never exceeds its fixed
capacity, and no stale prepare votes survive once the line has returned to
idle between rounds.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every admission round that begins eventually commits and
returns the line to idle, even though some station may be slow to cast its
vote.

---- MODULE W4Od14m9p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, Sectors, InitSector, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, loc, lastApplied, inflight, coverage

vars == <<epoch, loc, lastApplied, inflight, coverage>>

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the coordinator bumps epoch and broadcasts
\* per-drone reassignment orders into an unordered inflight set, so a drone
\* may observe and apply orders out of the sequence they were issued in.
\* coverage is the tracked "nothing created or destroyed" quantity: it must
\* always equal the true count of drones actually stationed at each sector,
\* even though ApplyOrder only ever sees the drone's CURRENT sector, never
\* the sector recorded by a stale, reordered order.

Messages == [drone: Drones, sector: Sectors, epoch: 1..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ loc \in [Drones -> Sectors]
  /\ lastApplied \in [Drones -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ inflight \subseteq Messages
  /\ coverage \in [Sectors -> 0..Cardinality(Drones)]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ loc = [d \in Drones |-> InitSector]
  /\ lastApplied = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ coverage = [s \in Sectors |-> IF s = InitSector THEN Cardinality(Drones) ELSE 0]

AdvanceEpoch ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<loc, lastApplied, inflight, coverage>>

BroadcastOrder(d, s) ==
  /\ epoch > 0
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[drone |-> d, sector |-> s, epoch |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, loc, lastApplied, coverage>>

\* Applies a still-fresh order. The sector it debits is the drone's current
\* loc, not the order's own bookkeeping, so reordering can never double
\* count or lose a unit of coverage.
ApplyOrder(d) ==
  \E m \in inflight :
    /\ m.drone = d
    /\ m.epoch > lastApplied[d]
    /\ LET old == loc[d] IN
         /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![d] = m.sector]
         /\ coverage' = IF old = m.sector
                         THEN coverage
                         ELSE [coverage EXCEPT ![old] = @ - 1, ![m.sector] = @ + 1]
    /\ lastApplied' = [lastApplied EXCEPT ![d] = m.epoch]
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A reordered order that a fresher order has already superseded is simply
\* dropped, never applied.
DiscardStale(d) ==
  \E m \in inflight :
    /\ m.drone = d
    /\ m.epoch <= lastApplied[d]
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, loc, lastApplied, coverage>>

Next ==
  \/ AdvanceEpoch
  \/ \E d \in Drones, s \in Sectors : BroadcastOrder(d, s)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : ApplyOrder(d)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : DiscardStale(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StateConstraint == Cardinality(inflight) <= 2

CoverageConservation ==
  \A s \in Sectors : coverage[s] = Cardinality({d \in Drones : loc[d] = s})

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Drones = {d1, d2, d3}
  Sectors = {s1, s2}
  InitSector = s1
  MaxEpoch = 2

INVARIANT CoverageConservation

CONSTRAINT StateConstraint
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm patrols a set of geographic sectors,
watching for new fire ignitions. A ground coordinator periodically declares
a new reconfiguration epoch and, within that epoch, broadcasts per-drone
reassignment orders telling an individual drone which sector to patrol next.
Because the drones communicate over a lossy mesh radio link, these broadcast
orders do not arrive in the order they were sent: they sit in a shared
in-flight pool and each drone may pick up and act on any order addressed to
it whenever it next has radio contact, regardless of when that order was
issued relative to other orders for the same drone. Every order carries the
epoch number it was issued in, and a drone only acts on an order if its
epoch is newer than the last one that drone actually applied; older,
superseded orders that arrive late are simply discarded. The system tracks,
for each sector, the number of drones the coordinator currently believes are
stationed there. The actions are: AdvanceEpoch, where the coordinator
advances the global epoch counter; BroadcastOrder, where the coordinator
places a fresh reassignment order for one drone and one destination sector
into the in-flight pool; ApplyOrder, where a drone picks up a still-fresh
order addressed to it, moves from its current sector to the order's
destination sector, and updates the per-sector coverage counts by debiting
the sector it is actually leaving (not whatever sector an older order might
have assumed it was in) and crediting the sector it is entering; and
DiscardStale, where a drone or the network drops an in-flight order whose
epoch has already been superseded by an order the drone already applied.
No drone is ever created or destroyed, and every drone patrols exactly one
sector at a time, so the coverage count is a conserved quantity: it can only
move between sectors one unit at a time as drones physically relocate, never
appear or vanish, even though the orders that drive those moves can arrive
out of order. SAFETY PROPERTY: for every sector, the coordinator's tracked
coverage count for that sector always equals the true number of drones
currently patrolling it, so that reordered reassignment orders never cause a
unit of coverage to be double-counted at one sector or dropped entirely
(this is the literal conservation-of-a-quantity property for this cell,
expressed as a per-sector coherence invariant rather than a single sum,
because coherence is what a reordering bug would actually break).

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Capacity, QCap

VARIABLES poolFree, backlogA, backlogB, activeA, activeB

vars == <<poolFree, backlogA, backlogB, activeA, activeB>>

\* Two robots (A, B) draw refill jobs from one shared depot pool of
\* Capacity crates; QCap bounds each robot's own queue (backpressure).
\* Enqueuing atomically reserves a crate from the shared pool so the two
\* independently-scheduled robots can never jointly reserve more crates
\* than the depot physically holds.

Init ==
  /\ poolFree = Capacity
  /\ backlogA = 0
  /\ backlogB = 0
  /\ activeA = 0
  /\ activeB = 0

EnqueueA ==
  /\ backlogA < QCap
  /\ poolFree > 0
  /\ backlogA' = backlogA + 1
  /\ poolFree' = poolFree - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlogB, activeA, activeB>>

EnqueueB ==
  /\ backlogB < QCap
  /\ poolFree > 0
  /\ backlogB' = backlogB + 1
  /\ poolFree' = poolFree - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlogA, activeA, activeB>>

StartA ==
  /\ backlogA > 0
  /\ activeA = 0
  /\ backlogA' = backlogA - 1
  /\ activeA' = 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolFree, backlogB, activeB>>

StartB ==
  /\ backlogB > 0
  /\ activeB = 0
  /\ backlogB' = backlogB - 1
  /\ activeB' = 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolFree, backlogA, activeA>>

CompleteA ==
  /\ activeA = 1
  /\ activeA' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolFree, backlogA, backlogB, activeB>>

CompleteB ==
  /\ activeB = 1
  /\ activeB' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolFree, backlogA, backlogB, activeA>>

\* Restock only fires at a synchronization checkpoint where both robots
\* are fully idle, avoiding a race between the robots' two views of the
\* shared pool.
Restock ==
  /\ backlogA = 0 /\ backlogB = 0 /\ activeA = 0 /\ activeB = 0
  /\ poolFree < Capacity
  /\ poolFree' = Capacity
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlogA, backlogB, activeA, activeB>>

Next == EnqueueA \/ EnqueueB \/ StartA \/ StartB \/ CompleteA \/ CompleteB \/ Restock

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(StartA) /\ WF_vars(CompleteA)
        /\ WF_vars(StartB) /\ WF_vars(CompleteB)

\* Safety: crates jointly reserved (queued + in-progress) by both robots
\* plus the pool's free count never exceed the fixed capacity -- once a
\* job is completed its crate has left the system (delivered), so the
\* accounted total can fall below capacity but never rise above it, and
\* the free count itself never goes negative.
CapacityConserved ==
  /\ poolFree >= 0
  /\ poolFree + backlogA + activeA + backlogB + activeB <= Capacity

\* Liveness: whenever a robot has outstanding work (queued or in
\* progress), that work is eventually fully drained -- no accepted job
\* is stuck forever.
JobsEventuallyServiced ==
  /\ (backlogA + activeA > 0) ~> (backlogA = 0 /\ activeA = 0)
  /\ (backlogB + activeB > 0) ~> (backlogB = 0 /\ activeB = 0)

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Capacity = 3
  QCap = 2
INVARIANT CapacityConserved
PROPERTY JobsEventuallyServiced
nl:
A vending machine network operates two independent restocking robots that
share a single bounded refill pool at a regional depot. The pool holds
crates of merchandise up to a fixed capacity. Each robot maintains its own
bounded work queue of accepted refill jobs (a job is a request to pull one
crate from the shared pool and deliver it to a machine); the queue enforces
backpressure by refusing to accept a new job once the robot's queue is full.
A robot can only enqueue a job while the shared pool has at least one crate
reserved on its behalf, and enqueuing a job atomically decrements the pool's
free-crate count so both robots can never together reserve more crates than
the pool actually holds. Once a robot dequeues a job to start work it moves
the job into an in-progress slot; completing the in-progress job delivers
the crate to a machine and frees up the robot's queue slot without changing
the pool (the crate already left the pool when the job was enqueued). The
pool is replenished by a depot restock action that adds crates back up to
capacity, which can only occur when both robots are momentarily idle at a
synchronization checkpoint (a natural pause used to avoid racing the two
robots' views of the pool). Because two independently-scheduled robots draw
from the one shared pool, a naive implementation could let their combined
reservations exceed the depot's physical capacity; this system instead
threads every enqueue through a single shared counter so the two queues can
never jointly overcommit it. The full action set is: RobotEnqueue(r) (robot
r accepts a new job into its queue if the queue has room and the pool has a
free crate), RobotStart(r) (robot r moves its oldest queued job into its
single in-progress slot if that slot is empty), RobotComplete(r) (robot r
finishes the in-progress job, delivering the crate and clearing the slot),
and DepotRestock (when both robots have empty queues and empty in-progress
slots, the pool is refilled to full capacity).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared pool's free-crate count never goes negative,
and the two robots' combined outstanding reservations (queued or
in-progress crates that have left the pool but not yet been delivered)
plus the free count never exceeds the depot pool's fixed capacity -- once
a job is completed its crate has been delivered and leaves the accounting
until the next restock, so the two independently-scheduled robots can
never together overcommit the pool.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every job a robot enqueues is eventually completed
(delivered to a machine and cleared from that robot's in-progress slot).

CONSTANTS Banks, MinCap, MaxCap, NoBank

ASSUME NoBank \notin Banks
ASSUME MinCap \in Nat /\ MaxCap \in Nat /\ MinCap <= MaxCap

VARIABLES lock, capacity, registered, requesting

Vars == <<lock, capacity, registered, requesting>>

  /\ lock \in Banks \cup {NoBank}
  /\ capacity \in MinCap..MaxCap
  /\ registered \subseteq Banks
  /\ requesting \subseteq Banks

  /\ lock = NoBank
  /\ capacity = MaxCap
  /\ registered = {}
  /\ requesting = {}

\* A bank joins the pool admitted under the current capacity bound.
Register(b) ==
  /\ b \in Banks \ registered
  /\ Cardinality(registered) < capacity
  /\ registered' = registered \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, capacity, requesting>>

Deregister(b) ==
  /\ b \in registered
  /\ lock # b
  /\ registered' = registered \ {b}
  /\ requesting' = requesting \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, capacity>>

RequestAcquire(b) ==
  /\ b \in registered \ requesting
  /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, capacity, registered>>

\* The compare-and-swap: succeeds only while the register reads free.
Acquire(b) ==
  /\ b \in requesting
  /\ lock = NoBank
  /\ lock' = b
  /\ requesting' = requesting \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, registered>>

Release(b) ==
  /\ lock = b
  /\ lock' = NoBank
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, registered, requesting>>

\* The regulator raises or lowers the admitted capacity at runtime.
ChangeCapacity(n) ==
  /\ n \in MinCap..MaxCap
  /\ n # capacity
  /\ capacity' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, registered, requesting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Register(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Deregister(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : RequestAcquire(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Acquire(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Release(b)
  \/ \E n \in MinCap..MaxCap : ChangeCapacity(n)

\* The CAS holder and every awaiting bank must stay inside the admitted pool.
HolderCoherence ==
  /\ (lock # NoBank => lock \in registered)
  /\ requesting \subseteq registered

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Banks = {b1, b2, b3}
  MinCap = 0
  MaxCap = 2
  NoBank = NoBank

INVARIANT HolderCoherence
nl:
A consortium of banks runs a shared interbank settlement batch process. Each
settlement cycle, a bank must first be admitted into the pool of registered
participants before it may compete for the single critical resource: the
shared settlement ledger that finalizes the batch. Admission is capped by a
capacity limit, and a regulator may raise or lower that capacity at runtime
in response to load conditions, changing how many banks may be registered
at once. A registered bank that wants to finalize the batch first records
its intent by requesting acquisition, then attempts to take ownership of
the ledger through a compare-and-swap register: the CAS only succeeds if
the register currently reads "free," and it atomically swaps in the
requesting bank's identity. A bank holding the ledger may release it,
returning the register to "free." A registered bank may also deregister
and leave the pool, but only once it no longer holds the ledger. The full
action set is: Register (a bank joins the capacity-admitted pool), Deregister
(a non-holding registered bank leaves the pool), RequestAcquire (a registered
bank signals intent to take the ledger), Acquire (the compare-and-swap that
grants the ledger to a requesting bank only while the register reads free),
Release (the holder returns the register to free), and ChangeCapacity (the
regulator adjusts the capacity bound at runtime). SAFETY PROPERTY: at every
reachable state the settlement ledger's CAS register names at most one
holder, and that holder together with every bank currently awaiting
acquisition remains inside the capacity-admitted pool of registered banks,
so that runtime capacity changes never strand a stale or unauthorized
claimant on the critical resource.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS T1, T2, B1, B2, MaxCap, MaxEpoch, NoBlock

Trains == {T1, T2}
Blocks == {B1, B2}

VARIABLES epoch, occupants, capacity, token, target

Vars == <<epoch, occupants, capacity, token, target>>

\* Each block's CAS register is its (epoch, occupants) pair; a train may
\* commit only by presenting a token equal to the block's CURRENT epoch.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in [Blocks -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ occupants \in [Blocks -> SUBSET Trains]
  /\ capacity \in [Blocks -> 1..MaxCap]
  /\ token \in [Trains -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ target \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {NoBlock}]

  /\ capacity = [b \in Blocks |-> MaxCap]
  /\ token = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
  /\ target = [t \in Trains |-> NoBlock]

\* presently in force there, even as capacity is reconfigured at runtime.

  /\ target[t] = NoBlock

  /\ \E b \in Blocks :
       /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![t] = epoch[b]]
       /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![t] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, occupants, capacity>>

Commit(t) ==
  /\ target[t] # NoBlock
  /\ token[t] = epoch[target[t]]
  /\ Cardinality(occupants[target[t]]) < capacity[target[t]]
  /\ occupants' = [occupants EXCEPT ![target[t]] = @ \cup {t}]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![t] = NoBlock]
  /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity>>

  /\ token[t] # epoch[target[t]]

  /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![t] = 0]

In a subway signalling block system, each track block is guarded by a
compare-and-swap register that pairs the block's authorized capacity with an
epoch counter. A train wishing to enter a block first prepares: it reads the
block's current epoch and stamps its own token with that value, recording the
block as its target. To actually occupy the block the train must commit: its
held token must still equal the block's live epoch, and the block must have
spare capacity below its currently authorized limit -- only then does the
compare-and-swap succeed and the train become an occupant. The signalling
operator may reconfigure a block's authorized capacity at runtime; doing so
immediately advances that block's epoch, so any token a train prepared before
the change is now stale and can never satisfy a later commit's compare step.
A train holding a stale token must abort, releasing its token and returning
to idle, rather than being allowed to occupy the block on outdated
authorization. A train already occupying a block may depart, freeing space
for a waiting train; a train may prepare a token for a new block only once
it holds no token and occupies no block itself. The full action set is:
Prepare (a train that is idle and occupies no block reads a target block's
epoch and stamps a token for that block), Commit (a train whose
token still matches its target block's epoch, and for which that block has
spare capacity, occupies the block), Abort (a train whose token no longer
matches its target block's epoch releases the token and returns to idle),
Depart (an occupying train leaves its block, freeing capacity), and
ChangeCapacity (the operator sets a block's authorized capacity at runtime
to any value no lower than that block's current occupancy, which advances
that block's epoch and stales any token outstanding for it). SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, the number of trains
occupying any block never exceeds that block's currently authorized
capacity, so no unauthorized or stale train can ever occupy a block beyond
the capacity presently in force there. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every train that
prepares a token for a block is eventually resolved -- it either commits and
occupies that block, or, on finding its token has gone stale, aborts and
returns to idle.

\* Two-phase commit over the warehouse robot fleet: the coordinator proposes a
\* batch, live participants vote, and commit needs unanimous yes with no
\* crash. The crasher never votes again, so every later round is forced to
\* abort -- that is what keeps the capacity bound safe despite the crash.

  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ votes = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ requested = 0

StartRound(amt) ==

  /\ amt \in RequestAmounts
  /\ requested' = amt
  /\ votes' = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
  /\ phase' = "collecting"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, crashed>>

Vote(p) ==
  /\ phase = "collecting"
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ votes[p] = "none"
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] =
                 IF reserved + requested <= CapacityBound THEN "yes" ELSE "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, phase, crashed, requested>>

CrashSilently(p) ==
  /\ phase = "collecting"
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ votes[p] = "none"
  /\ crashed' = {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, phase, votes, requested>>

DecideCommit ==
  /\ phase = "collecting"
  /\ AllLiveResponded
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ \A p \in Participants : votes[p] = "yes"
  /\ reserved' = reserved + requested
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed, requested>>

DecideAbort ==
  /\ phase = "collecting"
  /\ AllLiveResponded
  /\ (crashed # {} \/ \E p \in Participants : votes[p] = "no")
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, votes, crashed, requested>>

  \/ \E amt \in RequestAmounts : StartRound(amt)
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Vote(p)
  \/ \E p \in Participants : CrashSilently(p)
  \/ DecideCommit
  \/ DecideAbort

\* Every open-round yes vote must be consistent with the bound it certifies.
CapacityWithinBound ==

nl:
In a warehouse robot fleet, a small set of mobile robots act as participants
in a two-phase commit protocol that the fleet's coordinator runs whenever it
wants to admit a new batch of items into a shared staging zone with a fixed
capacity bound. Each round the coordinator proposes a batch size drawn from a
short list of standard request amounts; every participant robot then casts a
yes or no vote depending on whether admitting that batch would keep the
zone's total reserved capacity within the bound at the batch's current level.
The coordinator commits the reservation, adding the batch to the reserved
total, only if every participant has voted yes and no participant is known to
have crashed; otherwise it aborts the round and the reserved total is left
unchanged. As the twist, exactly one designated robot in the fleet may crash
silently before casting its vote: it never votes and never recovers, so from
that point on the coordinator can never again observe a unanimous yes across
all participants and must abort every subsequent round, trading throughput
for safety. The full action set is: starting a new round with a chosen batch
size, a live participant casting its vote, the one designated participant
crashing silently before it votes, the coordinator committing a round once
all live participants have voted yes and none has crashed, and the
coordinator aborting a round once all live participants have responded but
either some voted no or a participant has crashed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the staging zone's total reserved capacity never exceeds its
bound, and while a round is in progress no participant can be shown to have
voted yes if committing that round would have pushed the reserved total past
the bound.

CONSTANTS Participants, Slots, Crasher, MaxRetries

NoneVal == "none"

VARIABLES status, version, owner, readVersion, request, retries

vars == <<status, version, owner, readVersion, request, retries>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ status \in [Participants -> {"idle", "attempting", "done", "abandoned", "crashed"}]
    /\ version \in [Slots -> Nat]
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Participants \cup {NoneVal}]
    /\ readVersion \in [Participants -> Nat]
    /\ request \in [Participants -> Slots]
    /\ retries \in [Participants -> Nat]

Init ==
    /\ status = [p \in Participants |-> "idle"]
    /\ version = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NoneVal]
    /\ readVersion = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
    /\ request = [p \in Participants |-> CHOOSE s \in Slots : TRUE]
    /\ retries = [p \in Participants |-> 0]

\* Optimistic read: snapshot the slot's version before attempting the CAS commit.
StartAttempt(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "idle"
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
        /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![p] = s]
        /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version[s]]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "attempting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, retries>>

\* CAS succeeds only if the slot is still free and unchanged since the read.
Commit(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "attempting"
    /\ owner[request[p]] = NoneVal
    /\ version[request[p]] = readVersion[p]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![request[p]] = p]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![request[p]] = @ + 1]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readVersion, request, retries>>

\* CAS lost the race; retry with a fresh read while budget remains.
Retry(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "attempting"
    /\ (owner[request[p]] # NoneVal \/ version[request[p]] # readVersion[p])
    /\ retries[p] < MaxRetries
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, readVersion, request>>

\* Retry budget exhausted while still losing the CAS race: give up cleanly.
Abandon(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "attempting"
    /\ (owner[request[p]] # NoneVal \/ version[request[p]] # readVersion[p])
    /\ retries[p] >= MaxRetries
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "abandoned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, readVersion, request, retries>>

\* The twist: the designated Crasher can go silent at any point, never acting again.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ p = Crasher
    /\ status[p] \in {"idle", "attempting"}
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "crashed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, readVersion, request, retries>>

Terminating ==
    /\ \A p \in Participants : status[p] \in {"done", "abandoned", "crashed"}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

StartAttemptAny == \E p \in Participants : StartAttempt(p)
CommitAny == \E p \in Participants : Commit(p)
RetryAny == \E p \in Participants : Retry(p)
AbandonAny == \E p \in Participants : Abandon(p)

Next == StartAttemptAny \/ CommitAny \/ RetryAny \/ AbandonAny \/ Crash(Crasher) \/ Terminating

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(StartAttemptAny) /\ WF_vars(CommitAny)
             /\ WF_vars(RetryAny) /\ WF_vars(AbandonAny)

\* A participant that believes it holds a slot really is the recorded owner --
\* the optimistic CAS never lets two participants both come away "done" with
\* the same slot, so the same slot is never double-allocated.
OwnershipCoherent == \A p \in Participants : status[p] = "done" => owner[request[p]] = p

\* Every non-crashing participant's reservation attempt is eventually resolved
\* (won or abandoned), even though the Crasher may go silent forever.
AttemptsResolve ==
    \A p \in Participants \ {Crasher} :
        (status[p] = "attempting") ~> (status[p] \in {"done", "abandoned"})

    Slots = {s1, s2}
    Crasher = p3

INVARIANT OwnershipCoherent

PROPERTY AttemptsResolve
nl:
A library's online reservation system lets patrons claim a pickup slot for a
requested book using optimistic locking with retry instead of a blocking
lock: a patron reads the slot's current version number and owner, then tries
to commit the reservation with a compare-and-swap that only succeeds if
nobody else changed the slot since the read. Each patron starts idle, then
begins an attempt by picking a slot and snapshotting its version. If the
compare-and-swap finds the slot still free and unchanged, the attempt
commits and the patron becomes the recorded owner of that slot. If the
compare-and-swap loses the race (the slot was already taken or its version
moved), the patron retries with a fresh snapshot as long as a small retry
budget remains; once the budget is exhausted and the race is still lost, the
patron abandons the attempt instead of retrying forever. One designated
patron's client can crash silently at any point while idle or mid-attempt,
after which it never acts again -- it does not release anything and does not
notify anyone. The system must ensure that a patron who believes it holds a
slot really does hold it, so the same pickup slot is never handed out to two
different reservations even though several patrons may be racing the same
compare-and-swap and one of them may vanish mid-race. The actions are:
starting an attempt (reading a slot's version), committing via a successful
compare-and-swap, retrying after a lost race while budget remains,
abandoning after the retry budget is exhausted, and the designated patron's
silent crash. SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a patron's reservation attempt is
recorded as done, that patron is truly the slot's recorded owner, so no
pickup slot is ever double-allocated to two patrons.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every patron other than the one that may crash eventually
has its reservation attempt resolved -- either committed or abandoned --
even if the crash-prone patron goes silent forever.

ASSUME NoOne \notin Participants

TypeOK ==

  /\ fineOwner \in [Slots -> Participants \cup {NoOne}]

  /\ fineOwner = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
  /\ alloc = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
  /\ crashed = {}

\* Outer tier of the hierarchical lock: reserve the hub before touching the slot.
AcquireCoarseLock(p, s) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ coarseOwner[s] = NoOne
  /\ coarseOwner' = [coarseOwner EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineOwner, alloc, crashed>>

\* Inner tier: only the current coarse-lock holder may confirm the fine lock.
AcquireFineLock(p, s) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ coarseOwner[s] = p
  /\ fineOwner[s] = NoOne
  /\ fineOwner' = [fineOwner EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, alloc, crashed>>

Allocate(p, s) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ fineOwner[s] = p
  /\ alloc[s] = NoOne
  /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, crashed>>

Release(p, s) ==
  /\ alloc[s] = p
  /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ fineOwner' = [fineOwner EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ coarseOwner' = [coarseOwner EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* The twist: a controller can stop acting without releasing anything it held.
CrashSilently(p) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, alloc>>

\* Recovery: hand both locks to a live claimant and wipe any stale record in
\* the same step, so the old and new claim can never both look valid at once.
ReclaimAfterCrash(p, s) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ \/ coarseOwner[s] \in crashed
     \/ fineOwner[s] \in crashed
  /\ coarseOwner' = [coarseOwner EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ fineOwner' = [fineOwner EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Next ==
  \E p \in Participants, s \in Slots :
     \/ AcquireCoarseLock(p, s)
     \/ AcquireFineLock(p, s)
     \/ Allocate(p, s)
     \/ Release(p, s)
     \/ CrashSilently(p)
     \/ ReclaimAfterCrash(p, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: an allocation record for a slot only stands while that same
\* controller genuinely holds both lock tiers -- rules out a slot ever being
\* recognized as allocated to two controllers, including across a crash.
AllocCoherent ==
  \A s \in Slots :
    alloc[s] # NoOne => /\ fineOwner[s] = alloc[s]
                         /\ coarseOwner[s] = alloc[s]

compete to allocate access slots on shared door hardware. Each slot is
guarded by a two-tier hierarchical lock: a controller must first acquire a
coarse reservation lock on the slot's hub before it may acquire the fine
confirmation lock underneath it, and only once it holds both may it write an
allocation record claiming the slot. A controller releases a slot by
clearing the allocation record together with both locks in one step. The
twist is that a controller can crash silently at any time -- it simply stops
acting while still holding whatever locks and allocation record it had, with
no notification to the rest of the network. To keep the network from
wedging permanently on a crashed controller's slot, any other live
controller may run a reclaim step on a slot whose coarse or fine lock is
held by a crashed controller: the reclaim step hands both locks to the
reclaiming controller and clears any stale allocation record for that slot
in the same step, so a fresh allocation must be written from scratch before
the slot counts as allocated again. The full action set is: acquiring the
coarse lock, acquiring the fine lock, writing the allocation record,
releasing a slot, a controller crashing silently, and reclaiming a slot from
a crashed controller.

slot's allocation record is only ever valid while it is corroborated by that
same controller currently holding both the coarse and fine locks for the
slot, so no slot is ever double-allocated to two controllers at once.

    /\ expired' = expired \cup {c}

RenewLease(c) ==

    /\ expired' = expired \ {c}
    /\ leased' = leased \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, onRunway>>

    /\ expired' = expired \ {c}

nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator manages a fixed number of runway-capacity
tokens, one per takeoff slot the runway can support at a time. Aircraft draw
a token from the shared pool as a lease, which grants the right to use the
runway. Because coordination between the tower and an aircraft is
asynchronous, every granted lease carries an expiry timer: if the aircraft
has not yet moved onto the runway before the timer lapses, the lease is
flagged expired rather than revoked outright. Expiry is only a staleness
flag, not a failure verdict -- a slow aircraft (delayed by taxi congestion
or a stuck handoff) is not the same as one that has failed, so an expired
aircraft still holds its token and may either renew the lease, proving it is
merely slow and still active, or proceed straight onto the runway using the
expired lease. Once an aircraft is on the runway it eventually completes its
takeoff and departs, returning its token to the pool for reuse. The full
action set is: RequestLease (an aircraft draws a free token from the pool
and becomes leased), ExpireLease (a leased aircraft's timer lapses and its
token moves to the expired bucket without being lost), RenewLease (an
expired aircraft proves it is only slow and its token moves back to
leased), EnterRunway (a leased or expired aircraft moves onto the runway,
its token following it), and Depart (an aircraft on the runway finishes and
returns its token to the pool).

tokens is accounted for in exactly one of the pool, the leased aircraft, the
expired-but-not-evicted aircraft, or the aircraft currently on the runway,
so the total is conserved even while a lease sits expired because its
holder is merely slow rather than failed.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every aircraft that holds a token -- whether its lease is
currently active or merely expired -- eventually reaches the runway and
departs, handing its token back to the pool.

at a time. A car gains the right to enter the bay by acquiring a lease on
it: the lease is granted only while the bay is free, and it binds the car
to the bay until the car either finishes and releases the lease explicitly,
or the lease's expiry deadline (set at grant time, a fixed lease length
ahead of the shared discrete clock) is reached and the system reclaims it.
The twist is that a car's onboard controller can crash silently while it
holds the lease: the crash does not run any release logic, so the car's
status simply flips to crashed while the lease record still shows it as
the bay's owner, and the bay stays unusable by anyone else until the
system's reclaim action later notices the lease has expired and clears it.
The shared clock advances independently, one tick at a time, up to a
bounded horizon, and is the only thing that can make a lease eligible for
reclamation. The full action set is: Acquire (a car with no lease takes the
bay's lease if it is currently unowned, setting itself as owner, marking
its status as washing, and recording an expiry deadline as the current
clock plus a fixed lease length), Release (the owning car voluntarily gives
up the lease while it is washing, clearing ownership and returning its
status to idle), Crash (the owning car's controller silently fails while
washing, flipping its status to crashed without clearing ownership or the
lease record), Tick (the shared clock advances by one, bounded by a
maximum horizon), and Reclaim (once the clock has reached or passed the
current lease's expiry deadline, the system clears the ownership record and
resets the former owner's status to idle, regardless of whether that owner
had crashed or was still legitimately finishing up).
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, the set of cars whose status is
washing is always a subset of the single recorded lease owner, so the bay
is never occupied by a car that isn't the current lease holder and never
by more than one car at once, even across a silent crash and the eventual
reclaim of that crashed car's expired lease.

---- MODULE W4Od14m9p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, MaxEpoch

ASSUME Drones # {}
ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat /\ MaxEpoch > 1
ASSUME "none" \notin Drones

VARIABLES epoch, recordEpoch, recordDrone, submittedEpoch, ackedEpoch, slow

vars == <<epoch, recordEpoch, recordDrone, submittedEpoch, ackedEpoch, slow>>

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the coordinator stamps a fresh epoch and
\* drones resubmit readings tagged with it; a merely slow drone keeps its
\* right to resubmit later instead of being dropped from the swarm.

NoDrone == "none"

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ recordEpoch = 0
  /\ recordDrone = NoDrone
  /\ submittedEpoch = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ ackedEpoch = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ slow = [d \in Drones |-> FALSE]

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<recordEpoch, recordDrone, submittedEpoch, ackedEpoch, slow>>

SubmitStep(d) ==
  /\ submittedEpoch[d] < epoch
  /\ submittedEpoch' = [submittedEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, recordEpoch, recordDrone, ackedEpoch, slow>>

Submit == \E d \in Drones : SubmitStep(d)

CommitStep(d) ==
  /\ submittedEpoch[d] >= recordEpoch
  /\ recordEpoch' = submittedEpoch[d]
  /\ recordDrone' = d
  /\ ackedEpoch' = [ackedEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = submittedEpoch[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, submittedEpoch, slow>>

Commit == \E d \in Drones : CommitStep(d)

MarkSlowStep(d) ==
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![d] = ~slow[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, recordEpoch, recordDrone, submittedEpoch, ackedEpoch>>

MarkSlow == \E d \in Drones : MarkSlowStep(d)

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ Submit
  \/ Commit
  \/ MarkSlow

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Reconfigure)
  /\ WF_vars(Submit)
  /\ WF_vars(Commit)

\* SAFETY: an acknowledgment can never outrun what the record actually shows.
NoLostUpdates == \A d \in Drones : ackedEpoch[d] <= recordEpoch

\* LIVENESS: once the epoch settles, every drone -- slow or not -- catches up.
AllAcked == <>(epoch = MaxEpoch /\ (\A d \in Drones : ackedEpoch[d] = MaxEpoch))

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Drones = {d1, d2}
  MaxEpoch = 3

INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
PROPERTY AllAcked
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares one record of the fire's current
perimeter. The swarm is kept coherent through epoch-numbered reconfiguration:
whenever the swarm reorganizes -- a relay drone drops off the mesh, a new
drone joins, or the flight plan changes -- the coordinator stamps a fresh
epoch number, and every drone is expected to resubmit its most recent
perimeter reading tagged with that new epoch. A drone that is merely
experiencing radio delay or is temporarily out of line-of-sight is never
treated as failed and is never dropped from the swarm's membership; the
protocol does not wait for it, but it keeps the right to resubmit its latest
reading, tagged with whatever epoch is current when it finally can
communicate again. The coordinator folds a drone's submitted reading into
the shared record only when that reading is at least as fresh (same epoch
or newer) as what the record already reflects, and it then acknowledges
that drone up through the epoch it just committed. This prevents a merely
slow drone's late-arriving reading from ever silently overwriting the
record with stale data once a newer epoch's readings have already landed,
and it also means the slow drone's contribution is never permanently
discarded -- it is simply folded in whenever it catches up. The swarm
supports four actions: reconfiguring to advance the shared epoch number, a
drone submitting its latest perimeter reading tagged with the current
epoch, the coordinator committing a submitted reading that is fresh enough
into the shared record and acknowledging that drone, and marking a drone as
currently slow for observability only -- this marking never blocks,
excludes, or otherwise changes what any drone or the coordinator is allowed
to do. SAFETY PROPERTY: no drone is ever acknowledged for an epoch newer
than the epoch the shared record actually reflects at that moment, so a
slow drone's earlier acknowledged contribution can never be silently lost
behind a stale overwrite. LIVENESS PROPERTY: once reconfiguration settles
at its final epoch, every drone's reading -- including a reading from a
drone that was slow -- is eventually committed into the shared record and
acknowledged.
