---- MODULE W4Od19m5p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Books, Voters, Capacity

VARIABLES reservedA, reservedB, proposalType, proposalInst, proposalBook, votes

vars == <<reservedA, reservedB, proposalType, proposalInst, proposalBook, votes>>

\* Branches A and B share one Books pool; every reserve/release needs quorum.

Init ==
  /\ reservedA = {}
  /\ reservedB = {}
  /\ proposalType = "none"
  /\ proposalInst = "A"
  /\ proposalBook = CHOOSE b \in Books : TRUE
  /\ votes = {}

ProposeReserve(inst, book) ==
  /\ proposalType = "none"
  /\ book \notin (reservedA \cup reservedB)
  /\ proposalType' = "reserve"
  /\ proposalInst' = inst
  /\ proposalBook' = book
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedA, reservedB>>

ProposeRelease(inst, book) ==
  /\ proposalType = "none"
  /\ book \in (IF inst = "A" THEN reservedA ELSE reservedB)
  /\ proposalType' = "release"
  /\ proposalInst' = inst
  /\ proposalBook' = book
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedA, reservedB>>

CastVote(v) ==
  /\ proposalType # "none"
  /\ v \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedA, reservedB, proposalType, proposalInst, proposalBook>>

\* Commit fires only once a majority backs the proposal; reserving may not
\* push the shared pool over Capacity.
Commit ==
  /\ proposalType # "none"
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Voters)
  /\ IF proposalType = "reserve"
       THEN /\ Cardinality(reservedA \cup reservedB) < Capacity
            /\ IF proposalInst = "A"
                 THEN reservedA' = reservedA \cup {proposalBook}
                 ELSE reservedA' = reservedA
            /\ IF proposalInst = "B"
                 THEN reservedB' = reservedB \cup {proposalBook}
                 ELSE reservedB' = reservedB
       ELSE /\ IF proposalInst = "A"
                 THEN reservedA' = reservedA \ {proposalBook}
                 ELSE reservedA' = reservedA
            /\ IF proposalInst = "B"
                 THEN reservedB' = reservedB \ {proposalBook}
                 ELSE reservedB' = reservedB
  /\ proposalType' = "none"
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposalInst, proposalBook>>

Abort ==
  /\ proposalType # "none"
  /\ proposalType' = "none"
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedA, reservedB, proposalInst, proposalBook>>

Next ==
  \/ \E inst \in {"A", "B"}, book \in Books : ProposeReserve(inst, book)
  \/ \E inst \in {"A", "B"}, book \in Books : ProposeRelease(inst, book)
  \/ \E v \in Voters : CastVote(v)
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: the instances never overlap on a title, and combined reservations
\* across both never exceed the shared pool Capacity.
PoolCapacityCoherence ==
  /\ reservedA \cap reservedB = {}
  /\ Cardinality(reservedA \cup reservedB) <= Capacity

====
nl:
This system models a library book reservation service shared by two independent
branch instances, Branch A and Branch B, that both draw reservations from a
single shared pool of book titles bounded by a fixed physical capacity. Rather
than committing a change unilaterally, each branch first proposes an action and
must collect a strict majority of votes from a fixed committee of voting
members -- quorum voting -- before the pool's state actually changes. A branch
proposes to reserve a title that is not currently held by either branch, or to
propose releasing a title that it currently holds; committee members then cast
votes for the single pending proposal; once more than half the committee has
voted, the proposal commits, applying the reservation or release to whichever
branch initiated it and clearing the vote tally; a pending proposal may instead
be aborted (withdrawn) before it commits, which likewise clears the vote tally
so a new proposal can be raised. Because both branches draw from the same
shared pool, a title reserved through Branch A must never also be held by
Branch B, and the combined number of titles reserved across both branches must
never exceed the pool's capacity. The full action set is: ProposeReserve,
ProposeRelease, CastVote, Commit, and Abort.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A title reserved through Branch A is never simultaneously
reserved through Branch B, and the combined number of titles reserved across
both branches never exceeds the shared pool's capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od13m3p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxSeq

ASSUME Nodes # {}
ASSUME MaxSeq \in Nat /\ MaxSeq > 0

VARIABLES leader, nextSeq, msgs, version, record

vars == <<leader, nextSeq, msgs, version, record>>

NoLeader == "none"

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ nextSeq = 1
  /\ msgs = {}
  /\ version = 0
  /\ record = 0

\* A leaderless network elects any available machine.
Elect ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ \E n \in Nodes : leader' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSeq, msgs, version, record>>

\* Failover: the current leader can drop out at any time.
Fail ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ leader' = NoLeader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSeq, msgs, version, record>>

\* The leader stamps and sends the next update. Sequence numbers are never
\* reused or reset across a failover, so two leaders never collide.
Submit ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ nextSeq <= MaxSeq
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {nextSeq}
  /\ nextSeq' = nextSeq + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, version, record>>

\* Delivery is order-agnostic (msgs is a set, so the network may reorder
\* in-flight updates). A message only commits if it is newer than the
\* update already applied; a stale, reordered message is simply dropped,
\* which is what prevents lost updates under reordering.
Deliver ==
  /\ \E s \in msgs :
       /\ s > version
       /\ version' = s
       /\ record' = s
       /\ msgs' = msgs \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, nextSeq>>

Next == Elect \/ Fail \/ Submit \/ Deliver

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Elect) /\ WF_vars(Deliver) /\ SF_vars(Submit)

\* SAFETY: the visible record always matches the highest-numbered update
\* actually applied -- no applied update can ever be clobbered by a
\* later-arriving, lower-numbered (stale) message.
RecordCoherent == record = version

\* LIVENESS: every submitted update is eventually delivered and applied,
\* so the record eventually reaches the highest number ever submitted.
AllSubmittedEventuallyApplied == <>(version = MaxSeq)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
  MaxSeq = 3
INVARIANT RecordCoherent
PROPERTY AllSubmittedEventuallyApplied
nl:
A network of vending machines shares one authoritative record -- the running
tally of a shared inventory ledger -- that must stay consistent even though
only one machine is allowed to write it at a time. The machines use leader
election with failover: whenever there is no leader, any machine in the
network may become the new leader. The current leader can fail at any
moment (a coin jam, a power blip, a lost heartbeat), which drops it back to
no-leader and lets another machine take over. While it holds leadership, a
machine submits update messages for the shared record; each update it
originates is stamped with the next unused sequence number, and sequence
numbers are never reused or reset across a failover, so two different
leaders can never stamp two different updates with the same number. Once
submitted, an update becomes a message travelling across the network to the
shared record, and the network can reorder these messages in flight -- an
update stamped later can be delivered and observed before one stamped
earlier. To cope with that reordering, the shared record only accepts an
incoming update if its sequence number is strictly greater than the
sequence number of the update it currently holds; an update that arrives
after a newer one has already been applied is recognized as stale and is
discarded rather than being allowed to clobber the newer value. The full
action set is: Elect (an available machine becomes leader when there is
none), Fail (the current leader drops leadership at any time), Submit (the
leader stamps and sends the next update), and Deliver (a message in transit
is delivered to the shared record, applied only if it is newer than what is
already recorded, otherwise dropped as stale).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared record's visible value always matches the
sequence number of the highest-numbered update that has actually been
applied to it, so a reordered, lower-numbered message can never overwrite a
value that a higher-numbered update already established -- no update, once
applied, is ever lost to a late-arriving stale message.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Despite leader failover and message reordering, every
update that gets submitted is eventually delivered and applied to the
shared record, so the record's sequence number eventually reaches the
highest sequence number any leader ever submitted.

---- MODULE W4Od19m9p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Books, HardCap, MaxEpoch, OverrideBudget

VARIABLES epoch, capacity, reservations, overrideCount, adminEnabled

vars == <<epoch, capacity, reservations, overrideCount, adminEnabled>>

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: capacity never resets below books already held.
Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ capacity = HardCap
  /\ reservations = {}
  /\ overrideCount = 0
  /\ adminEnabled = FALSE

Reserve(b) ==
  /\ b \in Books
  /\ b \notin reservations
  /\ Cardinality(reservations) < capacity
  /\ reservations' = reservations \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, overrideCount, adminEnabled>>

Release(b) ==
  /\ b \in reservations
  /\ reservations' = reservations \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, overrideCount, adminEnabled>>

\* Admin override bypasses the soft cap, bounded by the hard cap and a per-epoch budget.
AdminOverrideReserve(b) ==
  /\ adminEnabled
  /\ overrideCount < OverrideBudget
  /\ b \in Books
  /\ b \notin reservations
  /\ Cardinality(reservations) < HardCap
  /\ reservations' = reservations \cup {b}
  /\ overrideCount' = overrideCount + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, adminEnabled>>

AdminRevoke(b) ==
  /\ adminEnabled
  /\ b \in reservations
  /\ reservations' = reservations \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, overrideCount, adminEnabled>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ capacity' \in (IF Cardinality(reservations) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE Cardinality(reservations))..HardCap
  /\ overrideCount' = 0
  /\ adminEnabled' \in BOOLEAN
  /\ UNCHANGED reservations

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Books : Reserve(b)
  \/ \E b \in Books : Release(b)
  \/ \E b \in Books : AdminOverrideReserve(b)
  \/ \E b \in Books : AdminRevoke(b)
  \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Held reservations stay under the hard cap; absent an override this
\* epoch, they also respect the epoch's own soft capacity.
CapacityInvariant ==
  /\ Cardinality(reservations) <= HardCap
  /\ (overrideCount = 0 => Cardinality(reservations) <= capacity)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Books = {1, 2, 3, 4}
    HardCap = 3
    MaxEpoch = 2
    OverrideBudget = 1
INVARIANT CapacityInvariant
nl:
A library operates a book reservation system over a fixed catalog of physical
copies. Time is organized into numbered epochs; each epoch carries its own
soft reservation capacity, and the library periodically reconfigures to the
next epoch, choosing a new soft capacity that can never be set below the
number of books currently reserved. Patrons may reserve an available book
only when the number of currently held reservations is strictly below the
current epoch's soft capacity, and they may release a reservation they hold
at any time. Separately, a privileged administrator may be authorized or
de-authorized at each reconfiguration; while authorized, the administrator
may issue a bounded number of override reservations per epoch that bypass
the epoch's soft capacity (though never past the system's absolute hard
capacity), and may also forcibly revoke any held reservation for
maintenance. The full action set is: Reserve(book), Release(book),
AdminOverrideReserve(book), AdminRevoke(book), and Reconfigure.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of held reservations never exceeds the
system's hard capacity limit, and whenever the administrator has not
exercised an override reservation in the current epoch, held reservations
also stay within that epoch's soft capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od9m8p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS f1, f2, f3, z1, z2, NoZone, NoFeeder, CapMin, CapMax, InitCap

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, decommissioned, capacity

Feeders == {f1, f2, f3}
Zones == {z1, z2}
ZoneOf == [f \in Feeders |-> IF f = f1 THEN z1 ELSE IF f = f2 THEN z1 ELSE z2]

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, decommissioned, capacity>>

\* Hierarchical locking: a controller must hold the coarse (zone) lock
\* before it may hold the fine (feeder) lock inside that zone.
\* decommissioned is the irreversible ledger: once a feeder is added, no
\* action may ever grant it the fine lock again.

Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = NoZone
    /\ fineLock = NoFeeder
    /\ decommissioned = {}
    /\ capacity = InitCap

AcquireCoarse(z) ==
    /\ coarseLock = NoZone
    /\ coarseLock' = z
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, decommissioned, capacity>>

AcquireFine(f) ==
    /\ fineLock = NoFeeder
    /\ coarseLock = ZoneOf[f]
    /\ f \notin decommissioned
    /\ fineLock' = f
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, decommissioned, capacity>>

Decommission ==
    /\ fineLock # NoFeeder
    /\ decommissioned' = decommissioned \cup {fineLock}
    /\ fineLock' = NoFeeder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, capacity>>

ReleaseFine ==
    /\ fineLock # NoFeeder
    /\ fineLock' = NoFeeder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, decommissioned, capacity>>

ReleaseCoarse ==
    /\ coarseLock # NoZone
    /\ fineLock = NoFeeder
    /\ coarseLock' = NoZone
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, decommissioned, capacity>>

AdjustCapacity ==
    /\ capacity' \in CapMin..CapMax
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, decommissioned>>

Next ==
    \/ \E z \in Zones : AcquireCoarse(z)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : AcquireFine(f)
    \/ Decommission
    \/ ReleaseFine
    \/ ReleaseCoarse
    \/ AdjustCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Decommission) /\ WF_vars(ReleaseFine) /\ WF_vars(ReleaseCoarse)

\* Coherence invariant for the safety property: the irreversible ledger and
\* the lock nesting can never disagree with each other.
DecommissionCoherence ==
    \A f \in Feeders :
        /\ (f \in decommissioned => fineLock # f)
        /\ (fineLock = f => coarseLock = ZoneOf[f])

\* Liveness: no feeder is left fine-locked forever; it is always eventually
\* decommissioned or the attempt is abandoned.
EventualRelease ==
    \A f \in Feeders : (fineLock = f) ~> (fineLock # f)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    f1 = f1
    f2 = f2
    f3 = f3
    z1 = z1
    z2 = z2
    NoZone = z0
    NoFeeder = f0
    CapMin = 0
    CapMax = 4
    InitCap = 2

INVARIANT DecommissionCoherence
PROPERTY EventualRelease
nl:
A power-grid load shedder manages a distribution network of feeders grouped
into zones. Decommissioning a feeder is an irreversible action that
permanently removes it from service, so the controller reaches it through
hierarchical locks: it must first take the coarse, zone-wide lock, and only
afterward may it take the fine-grained lock on a single feeder inside that
zone before it may commit the decommission. Grid capacity fluctuates at
runtime -- weather, maintenance windows, and demand swings raise or lower
the available capacity independently of the locking pipeline -- so the
controller may also abandon a fine-locked feeder without decommissioning it
if conditions no longer call for shedding, and it releases the zone-wide
lock once no feeder in that zone is still fine-locked. The system supports
six actions: AcquireCoarse (take the zone-wide lock when it is free),
AcquireFine (take the per-feeder lock on a feeder inside the held zone,
only if that feeder has not already been decommissioned), Decommission
(commit the irreversible removal of the currently fine-locked feeder and
release its fine lock), ReleaseFine (release the fine lock without
decommissioning, abandoning that attempt), ReleaseCoarse (release the
zone-wide lock once no feeder in it is fine-locked), and AdjustCapacity
(grid capacity moves to any value within its allowed range, independent of
the locking pipeline). SAFETY PROPERTY: once a feeder has been
decommissioned it can never again be granted the fine lock, and whenever a
feeder holds the fine lock, the zone containing it is the zone currently
holding the coarse lock -- both hold no matter how grid capacity changes at
runtime. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every feeder that acquires the fine lock is
eventually released from it, either by being decommissioned or by having
the attempt abandoned.

---- MODULE W4Od10m4p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS ReqIdsA, ReqIdsB, Cap

ReqIds == ReqIdsA \cup ReqIdsB

VARIABLES pool, queuedA, queuedB, authorized, done

vars == <<pool, queuedA, queuedB, authorized, done>>

\* Two independent signalling instances (A = northbound, B = southbound)
\* admit requests into one shared bounded work queue of capacity Cap; the
\* pool counter enforces backpressure across both instances at once.
\* Granting movement authority is the irreversible action: GrantOnce below
\* checks a granted request never returns to either queue and that
\* completion always follows a real grant, not the other way around.

Init ==
  /\ pool = 0
  /\ queuedA = {}
  /\ queuedB = {}
  /\ authorized = {}
  /\ done = {}

AdmitA(r) ==
  /\ r \in ReqIdsA
  /\ r \notin queuedA \cup queuedB \cup authorized \cup done
  /\ pool < Cap
  /\ queuedA' = queuedA \cup {r}
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queuedB, authorized, done>>

AdmitB(r) ==
  /\ r \in ReqIdsB
  /\ r \notin queuedA \cup queuedB \cup authorized \cup done
  /\ pool < Cap
  /\ queuedB' = queuedB \cup {r}
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queuedA, authorized, done>>

GrantA(r) ==
  /\ r \in queuedA
  /\ queuedA' = queuedA \ {r}
  /\ authorized' = authorized \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, queuedB, done>>

GrantB(r) ==
  /\ r \in queuedB
  /\ queuedB' = queuedB \ {r}
  /\ authorized' = authorized \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, queuedA, done>>

Complete(r) ==
  /\ r \in authorized \ done
  /\ done' = done \cup {r}
  /\ pool' = pool - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queuedA, queuedB, authorized>>

\* AllDone lets the shared queue reach a quiescent terminal state (every
\* request finished) without TLC reporting a spurious deadlock there.
AllDone == \A r \in ReqIds : r \in done

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in ReqIdsA : AdmitA(r)
  \/ \E r \in ReqIdsB : AdmitB(r)
  \/ \E r \in ReqIdsA : GrantA(r)
  \/ \E r \in ReqIdsB : GrantB(r)
  \/ \E r \in ReqIds : Complete(r)
  \/ (AllDone /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* GrantOnce is the safety property: authorization is one-way. A request
\* that has been granted must never reappear in either instance's shared
\* admission queue, and a request cannot be completed unless it was
\* actually granted authority first.
GrantOnce ==
  /\ \A r \in ReqIds : (r \in authorized) => (r \notin queuedA /\ r \notin queuedB)
  /\ \A r \in ReqIds : (r \in done) => r \in authorized

====
nl: In a subway signalling block system, two independent interlocking instances -- one governing the northbound approach and one governing the southbound approach to a shared junction -- issue movement authorities that let a train enter a track block. Because both approaches feed the same physical junction, they draw admission slots from one shared bounded work queue: at most Cap requests may be admitted (queued, awaiting authorization) at any time regardless of which instance they came from, and further requests are refused once the queue is full (backpressure). Once an instance's request has been admitted, that instance may grant it a movement authority, which is irreversible -- a train given authority to enter the block can never be un-authorized or re-queued for a fresh authority. After a train completes its move through the block, its request is marked done and its shared slot is released back to the pool for either instance's future requests. The system's five actions are: admitting a request from the northbound instance into the shared queue when capacity remains (AdmitA), admitting a request from the southbound instance into the shared queue when capacity remains (AdmitB), granting movement authority to an admitted northbound request (GrantA), granting movement authority to an admitted southbound request (GrantB), and marking a granted request complete and releasing its shared slot back to the pool (Complete). SAFETY PROPERTY: even though both signalling instances draw admission slots from one shared pool, a request's movement authority, once granted, is never re-queued by either instance, and no request is ever marked complete before it has actually been granted authority.

---- MODULE W4Od16m3p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, NoLeader, Cap, N

\* Leader election with failover over a small station cluster: exactly one
\* online station may hold the leader role and admit prescription requests
\* into a capacity-bounded staging area. The submission pool is a set (not
\* a sequence), modeling a network that can deliver requests out of order;
\* filling always drains the lowest-numbered staged id first, so admission
\* reordering can never let a later request permanently outrun an earlier
\* one still waiting to be filled.

VARIABLES leader, alive, requests, pending, dispensed

vars == <<leader, alive, requests, pending, dispensed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ alive \subseteq Nodes
    /\ requests \subseteq 1..N
    /\ pending \subseteq 1..N
    /\ dispensed \subseteq 1..N

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ alive = Nodes
    /\ requests = 1..N
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ dispensed = {}

Elect ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ \E n \in alive : leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, requests, pending, dispensed>>

Fail ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ leader \in alive
    /\ alive' = alive \ {leader}
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requests, pending, dispensed>>

Recover ==
    /\ \E n \in Nodes \ alive : alive' = alive \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, requests, pending, dispensed>>

Admit ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ requests # {}
    /\ Cardinality(pending) < Cap
    /\ \E r \in requests :
        /\ requests' = requests \ {r}
        /\ pending' = pending \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, dispensed>>

Dispense ==
    /\ pending # {}
    /\ LET s == CHOOSE m \in pending : \A o \in pending : m <= o
       IN /\ pending' = pending \ {s}
          /\ dispensed' = dispensed \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, requests>>

Next == Elect \/ Fail \/ Recover \/ Admit \/ Dispense

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Dispense)

\* Capacity is never exceeded, the three id-groups that partition 1..N
\* never overlap, and a held leader role always belongs to an online node.
CapacityInvariant ==
    /\ Cardinality(pending) <= Cap
    /\ pending \cap dispensed = {}
    /\ pending \cap requests = {}
    /\ dispensed \cap requests = {}
    /\ (leader # NoLeader => leader \in alive)

\* Every admitted (still-pending) request eventually gets filled, even
\* though admission order and leader identity can both keep changing.
EventualDispense == \A s \in 1..N : (s \in pending) ~> (s \in dispensed)

nl:
A pharmacy operates a small cluster of dispenser stations that fill
prescriptions from a shared, capacity-limited staging area. Exactly one
station holds the "leader" role at a time: only the leader may pull a new
prescription request out of the submission pool and admit it into the
staging area, where it waits to be filled. Stations can go offline (the
leader included) and later come back online; when the leader goes offline it
immediately relinquishes the role, and any station that is online and sees
no leader may take over -- this is the leader-election-with-failover
mechanism that keeps the pharmacy operating despite a station dropping out
mid-shift. The pharmacy's network delivers submitted prescription requests
out of order relative to how they were dropped off, so the leader may admit
request #5 before request #2 even though #2 arrived first; the staging area
therefore is not a queue but an unordered pool of admitted-but-unfilled
request ids. To keep the physical staging area from overflowing, the leader
may not admit a new request while the staging area already holds its
maximum capacity of unfilled prescriptions. Once a request is admitted,
filling always proceeds by lowest request id first, so the reordering during
admission never lets a later request permanently jump ahead of an earlier
one still waiting to be filled. The full action set is: Elect (an online
station takes over an empty leader role), Fail (the current leader drops
offline and the role becomes empty), Recover (an offline station comes back
online), Admit (the leader pulls one request from the submission pool into
the staging area, only if the staging area is below capacity), and Dispense
(the lowest-numbered request currently in the staging area is filled and
removed).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the staging area never holds more unfilled prescriptions
than its capacity, its contents never overlap with the submission pool or
the already-filled set, and whenever a station holds the leader role that
station is actually online.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every prescription request that is admitted into the
staging area is eventually filled and removed, regardless of how many times
leader failover occurs or how out-of-order requests were admitted.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Participants, MaxQueue, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES queue, epoch, authorized, acted, droppedCount

vars == <<queue, epoch, authorized, acted, droppedCount>>

(* Scan requests wait in a bounded SET-queue; Route may pull any pending  *)
(* one rather than the oldest, modeling reordering on the mesh network.  *)
(* Revoking or granting always advances the epoch, so a stale (reordered) *)
(* request is told apart from a fresh one by comparing its stamp to it.  *)

Init ==
  /\ queue = {}
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ authorized = Participants
  /\ acted = {}
  /\ droppedCount = 0

Submit(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ Cardinality(queue) < MaxQueue
  /\ [p |-> p, e |-> epoch] \notin queue
  /\ [p |-> p, e |-> epoch] \notin acted
  /\ queue' = queue \cup {[p |-> p, e |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorized, acted, droppedCount>>

Revoke(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ authorized' = authorized \ {p}
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, acted, droppedCount>>

Grant(p) ==
  /\ p \notin authorized
  /\ authorized' = authorized \cup {p}
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, acted, droppedCount>>

Route ==
  \E m \in queue :
    /\ queue' = queue \ {m}
    /\ acted' = acted \cup {m}
    /\ IF m.e = epoch
       THEN UNCHANGED droppedCount
       ELSE droppedCount' = droppedCount + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorized>>

Next == (\E p \in Participants : Submit(p) \/ Revoke(p) \/ Grant(p)) \/ Route

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Revoke/Grant stay enabled forever (no deadlock); this just bounds     *)
(* the model-checked epoch range.                                        *)
StateConstraint == epoch <= MaxEpoch

(* Safety: a still-queued request is from a currently authorized handler *)
(* or is already strictly behind the epoch -- Route can only drop it.    *)
QueueAuthorizationCoherence ==
  \A m \in queue : m.p \in authorized \/ m.e < epoch

nl:
At a major international airport, a baggage router directs suitcases arriving
from check-in kiosks and connecting flights toward the correct sorting
carousel. Requests to route a bag are produced by handheld scanners carried by
baggage handlers (the participants) and are held in a small bounded work
queue before the router acts on them; when the queue is already at capacity,
new scan requests are refused outright as backpressure rather than being
accepted and left to pile up. The airport's security office periodically
revokes a handler's scanning credential (for example, after a shift ends or a
device is reported lost) and can later re-grant a fresh credential to the
same handler; every such change advances a single system-wide authorization
epoch. Because scan requests travel over the airport's wireless mesh network,
they can be reordered and delayed in transit, so a request that was queued
while a handler was authorized can still be sitting in the queue after that
handler's credential has since been revoked, or revoked and then re-granted.
The router only acts on a queued request if the authorization epoch has not
advanced since the request was stamped; any request that surfaces after the
epoch has moved on is silently dropped and never acted upon. The full action
set is: a handler submits a scan request (subject to queue capacity and
current authorization); security revokes a handler's credential (which also
advances the epoch); security grants, or re-grants, a handler's credential
(which also advances the epoch); and the router pulls an arbitrary pending
request from the queue and either confirms it or drops it, depending on
whether its stamped epoch is still current. SAFETY PROPERTY: every request
still waiting in the queue must either belong to a handler who is currently
authorized, or carry an epoch stamp that already lags strictly behind the
current epoch, so the router can never confirm a request from an
unauthorized or stale (reordered) participant -- it can only ever drop one.
